title: Login's Apple button holds up at narrow widths and in a light theme, and its busy test leaves no stub behind
acceptance: With Login's form column narrower than about 220 px (for example 175% page zoom on a 375 px phone), the Apple button clips neither its title nor the logo's left edge, and it still follows Apple's rules: Apple's logo file at the button's full height, never cropped or padded, at least 140 px wide, and one of Apple's titles at rest ("Continue with Apple"). While busy it either keeps today's "Opening Apple sign-in…", unclipped, or keeps "Continue with Apple" and shows the busy state through aria-busy, disabled and an indicator outside the title.
Where the light theme is on ([data-theme="light"]), the white Apple button has a visible outline against the light page, as Apple's white-with-outline style does; the dark default is unchanged.
Login.test.tsx's busy-state test leaves no never-resolving signInSocial stub for later tests (mockReturnValueOnce, or a reset the shared afterEach runs), and the file still passes.

evidence.summary: #783's final review, non-significant note 1: (a) Login.tsx:342, with a form column under about 220 px the fixed-height, no-wrap button clips "Opening Apple sign-in…" and the logo's left edge; (b) no outline on the white button if a light theme is turned on; (c) the busy-state test's never-resolving signInSocial stub is not reset by vi.clearAllMocks(), so a later Apple-click test would hang.

#784's final review, notes 2 to 4: the next action lacked its Backlog boundary; acceptance 1 asked for the busy title unclipped and for one of Apple's titles, which the busy title is not; viewport emulation sets the width, not the page zoom. Corrected here.

Builder, batch #805: Login.test.tsx passes (22 tests). The busy-state test uses mockReturnValueOnce and a following test proves no signInSocial stub is left; two more assert the title's container-scaled size classes (rest and busy) and the light-theme outline overlay.

Builder, Chromium viewport emulation against the Vite dev server with the API mocked: at 140, 180, 214, 260, 320, 390 and 1440 px wide, at rest and busy, the Apple button's title and the logo's left edge are unclipped, the logo is 31x44 in a 44 px button at least 140 px wide, and the page does not scroll sideways from 180 px up. At 214 px the form column is 174 px and the title is 11 px at rest, 9.4 px busy; it is 16 px from a 230 px button (265 px busy). With data-theme=light set by hand the outline overlay shows; in the dark default it is display:none.

resolution: The Apple button is a size container and its title's font size scales with the button's width (1rem at normal widths, smaller only when the button is under about 230 px, or 265 px while busy), so neither "Continue with Apple" nor "Opening Apple sign-in…" clips down to Apple's 140 px minimum; safe centring keeps the logo's left edge in view. Where [data-theme="light"] is on, an overlay draws a 1 px black outline without padding the logo; the dark default is unchanged. The busy test's stub is now once-only. Nothing in the app sets data-theme yet, so the outline was checked by setting the attribute by hand.
